source: NCERT Class VIII, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 4.

sections.heading: 1. Effects of Electric Current
points: An electric current can produce a **heating effect**, a **magnetic effect** and a **chemical effect**.
This chapter focuses on the **magnetic and heating** effects.
Current flows only in a **closed circuit**.

sections.heading: 2. Heating Effect
points: Current flowing through a wire makes it **hot** — the heating effect.
**Higher resistance → more heat**; devices like **heaters, irons, toasters, geysers** use high-resistance **nichrome** wire; bulbs use a **tungsten** filament.
An **electric fuse** is a safety device — a thin wire that **melts and breaks the circuit** if the current is too large, preventing fire.

sections.heading: 3. Magnetic Effect
points: A current-carrying wire behaves like a **magnet** (discovered by **Oersted**) — it deflects a nearby **compass**.
An **electromagnet** = a coil of wire around an **iron core**; it acts as a magnet **only when current flows** and can be made very strong.
Uses of electromagnets: **cranes (to lift iron), electric bells, motors, loudspeakers**.

sections.heading: 4. The Electric Bell
points: Works on the **magnetic effect**: current magnetises the electromagnet → it pulls an iron strip → the hammer strikes the gong → this **breaks the circuit** → magnet loses power → strip springs back → circuit completes again → the process repeats and the bell rings.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Heating effect: heater/iron/toaster (nichrome); bulb filament = tungsten; fuse = safety device.
Magnetic effect (Oersted): current-carrying wire acts as a magnet, deflects a compass.
Electromagnet = coil on iron core; magnetic only when current flows; used in cranes/bells/motors.
Electric bell works on the magnetic effect.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: A **fuse** melts to **break** the circuit and prevent fire.
An **electromagnet** is magnetic **only while current flows** (unlike a permanent magnet).
The **magnetic effect** was discovered by **Oersted** (compass deflection).
The **electric bell** uses the **magnetic** effect; heaters use the **heating** effect.
